questions.stem: Two triangles are congruent if they have:

options.text: Exactly the same shape and size
The same angles but different side lengths

questions.explanation: Congruent triangles are identical in shape and size. All corresponding sides and angles are equal. Having the same area or perimeter alone is not sufficient.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a valid condition for proving two triangles are congruent?

options.text: SSA (two sides and a non-included angle)
SAS (two sides and the included angle)

questions.explanation: SAS (Side-Angle-Side) is a valid congruence condition. AAA only proves similarity, not congruence. SSA is not a valid condition as it can produce two different triangles (the ambiguous case).
